entities.summary:
Fiacha Cennfinnán, son of Starn, son of Rudraige, became High King of Ireland when he overthrew his great-uncle Sengann in 1st-century BCE Ireland. This event marked the beginning of a new era for the Fir Bolg kingdom and had significant implications for the future trajectory of Irish history. The overthrow of Sengann led to a period of instability, during which the Fir Bolg faced challenges from neighboring tribes and eventually succumbed to the rising power of the Tuatha Dé Danann.

Fiacha Cennfinnán's reign was also marked by his efforts to consolidate power and secure alliances with neighboring kingdoms. He is remembered in Irish mythology as a key figure who played a crucial role in shaping the course of Irish history during this pivotal period.

The legacy of Fiacha Cennfinnán can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Tuatha Dé Danann, who would go on to shape the mythology and culture of Ireland for centuries to come. His actions had a lasting impact on the political landscape of Ireland, paving the way for the eventual arrival of the Milesians and the establishment of the Gaelic kingdoms.

The story of Fiacha Cennfinnán serves as a reminder of the complex web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that characterized ancient Irish history. As such, it offers valuable insights into the cultural, social, and political dynamics of this fascinating period.

entities.summary:
Fiacha Cennfinnán, son of Starn, son of Rudraige, of the Fir Bolg, became High King of Ireland when he overthrew his great-uncle Sengann in 1125 BCE. This event marked a pivotal shift in Irish mythology and politics.

As High King, Fiacha Cennfinnán implemented various reforms aimed at strengthening the power of the Fir Bolg and expanding their territories. He also established trade relationships with neighboring tribes and expanded Ireland's borders through strategic alliances.

Despite his significant contributions to Irish history, Fiacha Cennfinnán's reign was cut short when he was killed in battle against the Tuatha Dé Danann in 1122 BCE. His legacy lived on, however, as his descendants continued to play important roles in Irish politics and mythology.

One of the most enduring legacies of Fiacha Cennfinnán is the Fir Bolg's distinctive cultural practices, which blended elements of ancient Celtic and pre-Christian traditions with influences from neighboring tribes and empires. This unique cultural synthesis would go on to shape the development of Irish identity and inform the country's rich artistic and literary heritage.

Fiacha Cennfinnán's story has been passed down through generations in Irish folklore, where he is remembered as a powerful and wise leader who expanded Ireland's borders and strengthened its people. His legacy continues to inspire and captivate audiences to this day.
